will allow you to directly call any functions in the function R script directly:
 Any functions can be directly called using 'lpsn_utils$<function name>',
 e.g., 

```{r setup, include=FALSE}

# Global set up: Show code blocks but don't run them by default when knitting

if (file.exists("LPSN_API_functions.R")) { 
  lpsn_utils <- new.env()
  sys.source("LPSN_API_functions.R", envir = lpsn_utils)
}


```

# Prepare data for LPSN API


__Install LPSN package and load library__

## Import and split combined taxa tables

_Check file formats_

Import file and check data structure (eg Best_taxonomy.csv from AGRF). Split any combined columns and eliminate unwanted columns.


```{r}

# check column name and first row before importing
readr::read_delim(
  file = "./data/Test_taxonomy.csv", # path where taxonomy file is located
  n_max = 1)

# ── Column specification ────────────────────────
# Delimiter: ","
# chr (3): Feature ID, Taxon, Assignment Database
# dbl (1): Confidence
# 
# ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
# ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.
# # A tibble: 1 × 4
#   `Feature ID`   Taxon    Confidence  `Assignment Database`
#   <chr>                            <chr>                                            <dbl> <chr>                
# 1 0005978dc14cfa9fd7b559b7721bf193 d__Bacteria; p__Bacteroidota; c__Bacteroid…         95 GTDB r207     
  
  
# import file - only import wanted columns (`Feature ID`& Taxon)
raw_taxa <- readr::read_delim(
  file = "./data/Test_taxonomy.csv", # path to where AGRF taxonomy file is
  delim = ",", # columns are separated by commas
  # select only Feature ID and Taxon columns
  col_select = c("Feature ID", "Taxon"), 
  trim_ws = TRUE  # get rid of preceding and trailing white spaces
) |> 
  ## Set the first column containing ASVs as row names
  tibble::column_to_rownames(var = "Feature ID")

nrow(raw_taxa)
# [1] 1080

## view data - truncated to max of 20 characters
subset <- utils::head(raw_taxa)

# Function: Truncate each cell to 10 characters
subset[] <- lapply(subset, function(col) {
  
  # Convert to character, then truncate to 20 characters
  substr(as.character(col), 1, 20)
})

# Print result
print(subset, quote = FALSE, right = FALSE)

# Taxonony in Taxon column separated by semicolons            
                                 Taxon               
# 0005978dc14cfa9fd7b559b7721bf193 d__Bacteria; p__Bact
# 000a91f2e03d19b50ee4c7b2671054b6 d__Bacteria; p__Plan
# 000a95ae83d53c8a196b707c5e1dcfa6 d__Bacteria; p__Plan
# 000c1766c74a33f3cf38892dec91d664 d__Bacteria; p__Firm
# 001a898130b235a2d574339155c929e7 d__Bacteria; p__Firm
# 001dc02a5297ea9c762ef03546a4a6f4 d__Bacteria; p__Acti


# separate taxa into individual columns
                                 
taxtable <- raw_taxa |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("ASV") |>   # keep ASVs as a column
  tibble::as_tibble() |>
  tidyr::separate(taxonomy,
                  sep = ";",
                  c("Domain",
                    "Phylum",
                    "Class",
                    "Order",
                    "Family",
                    "Genus",
                    "Species")
                  ) |>
  # remove preceding and trailing white spaces
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.character), stringr::str_trim)) |>
  # restore ASVs as rownames
  tibble::column_to_rownames("ASV") |>   
  as.matrix()

# check variable names
colnames(taxtable)
# [1] "Domain"  "Phylum"  "Class"   "Order"   "Family"  "Genus"   "Species"


# check what the prefixes look like
# Show rows 1 to 3 and columns 1 and 3
utils::head(taxtable)[1:3,1:2]



## remove prefix for taxa names with functions saved in:
# LPSN_API_functions.R
taxtable_df <- lpsn_utils$remove_taxa_prefix(taxtable)
colnames(taxtable_df)
# [1] "Domain"  "Phylum"  "Class"   "Order"   "Family"  "Genus"   "Species"

# check data
subset <- utils::head(taxtable_df)

# Truncate each cell to 10 characters
subset[] <- lapply(subset, function(col) {
  
  # Convert to character, then truncate
  substr(as.character(col), 1, 20)
})

# check prefixes are gone
utils::head(subset)[1:3,1:2] # print out row 1:3 and col 1:2


# remove excess white spaces
df_clean <- taxtable_df |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.character), stringr::str_trim))

# save objects 

## save taxonomy with prefixes removed
saveRDS(df_clean, file = "./objects/taxa.dataframes.precleaned.noprefix.rds") # path to save objects


```



_Prepare data for taxonomy assignment_

Check for mitochondria and chloroplasts. 
If found, remove from data

```{r}

### load object to be checked
df_clean <- readRDS(file = "./objects/taxa.dataframes.precleaned.noprefix.rds")

# Count occurrences of chloroplast or mitochondria in each column
counts <- df_clean |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::everything(),
      as.character
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::everything(),
      ~ sum(
        stringr::str_detect(
          .,
          stringr::regex(
            "chloroplast|mitochondri", 
            ignore_case = TRUE)
        ),
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    )
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = dplyr::everything(),
    names_to = "Taxonomic_level",
    values_to = "Count"
  )

print(counts)

#  Taxonomic_level Count
#   <chr>           <int>
# 1 Domain              0
# 2 Phylum              0
# 3 Class               0
# 4 Order               0
# 5 Family              0
# 6 Genus               0
# 7 Species             0


# no mitochondrion or chloroplasts - no need for modification 


```


_Removing unwanted ASVs_

Remove chloroplasts and mitochondria if present

```{r}

# Set search criteria
pattern <- "chloroplast|mitochondri"

# # select rows that match criteria
mito_chloro <- df_clean %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("row_name") |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::if_any(
    dplyr::everything(), ~ base::grepl(pattern, .x, ignore.case = TRUE)))

utils::head(mito_chloro)



# remove the mito/chloroplast ASVs from df_clean dataframe
df_filtered <- df_clean[!base::rownames(df_clean) %in% mito_chloro$row_name, ]

# check that you only removed the required 

base::nrow(df_clean)

base::nrow(df_filtered)

base::nrow(mito_chloro)

base::nrow(df_clean) - base::nrow(df_filtered)


## save taxonomy with prefixes removed
saveRDS(df_filtered, file = "./objects/taxa.dataframes.precleaned.noprefix.rds")
```

```{r}


# load data if starting in this block:
df_clean <- readRDS(file = "./objects/taxa.dataframes.precleaned.noprefix.rds")

# number of empty cells for each taxonomic level

df_clean |>
```

## Clean taxa names

LPSN does not contain place holder names (numbers and letters). Need to clean up the taxa names that are only made up of letters and remove suffixes added by AGRF.

Any taxa names with numbers will need manual curation, so you will need to decide how you want to clean your data - the LPSN API call will result in a record in the log for failed searches.

__Load Data__

```{r}

df_clean <- readRDS(file = "./objects/taxa.dataframes.precleaned.noprefix.rds")

```


### STEP 1: Remove underscores and initial orphaned letter codes

Check all columns and remove underscores, and any resulting single and double orphaned letters in columns with no numbers - means that the majority of the Species column will not be changed


```{r}

# Remove underscores and orphaned letters but it ignores anything with numbers
## will not clean all orphans - need to do a column by column check after this

df_trimmed <- df_clean |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(
    c(Domain, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species),
    ~ ifelse(
      stringr::str_detect(.x, "^[^0-9]+$"),  # TRUE only if NO numbers anywhere
      .x |>
        stringr::str_replace_all("_", " ") |>
        stringr::str_remove_all("\\b[A-Za-z]{1,2}\\b") |>
        stringr::str_squish(),
      .x  # leave untouched if ANY number is present
    )
  ))


head(df_trimmed)

#     Domain          Phylum           Class               Order
# 1 Bacteria    Bacteroidota     Bacteroidia     Chitinophagales
# 2 Bacteria Planctomycetota  Planctomycetia       Isosphaerales
# 3 Bacteria Planctomycetota  Planctomycetia       Isosphaerales
# 4 Bacteria      Firmicutes         Bacilli          Bacillales
# 5 Bacteria      Firmicutes         Bacilli          Bacillales
# 6 Bacteria  Actinobacteria Thermoleophilia Solirubrobacterales
#                 Family           Genus
# 1     Chitinophagaceae    Segetibacter
# 2       Isosphaeraceae    Unclassified
# 3       Isosphaeraceae        Tautonia
# 4          Bacillaceae        Bacillus
# 5     Amphibacillaceae    Unclassified
# 6 Solirubrobacteraceae Solirubrobacter
#                             Species
# 1           Segetibacter aerophilus
# 2                      Unclassified
# 3                    Tautonia rosea
# 4                Bacillus foraminis
# 5                      Unclassified
# 6 Solirubrobacter ginsenosidimutans


# the number of rows should remain the same
sprintf("%d : %d", nrow(df_clean), nrow(df_trimmed))
# [1] "1080 : 1080"

## check row changes for record 705
# Transpose the combined rows
comparison <- t(rbind(df_clean[705, ], df_trimmed[705, ]))
colnames(comparison) <- c("Original", "Trimmed")

comparison

#         Original                            Trimmed                            
# Domain  "Bacteria"                          "Bacteria"                         
# Phylum  "Proteobacteria"                    "Proteobacteria"                   
# Class   "Alphaproteobacteria"               "Alphaproteobacteria"              
# Order   "Sphingomonadales"                  "Sphingomonadales"                 
# Family  "Sphingomonadaceae"                 "Sphingomonadaceae"                
# Genus   "Sphingoaurantiacus"                "Sphingoaurantiacus"               
# Species "Sphingoaurantiacus polygranulatus" "Sphingoaurantiacus polygranulatus"



# save trimmed object

saveRDS(df_trimmed, file = "./objects/taxa.dataframes.precleaned.trimmed.rds")

```



### STEP 2: Clean Species column (if populated)

Check if any single, double or triple string in species column.
Look for a space, exactly one uppercase letter, followed by a space or the end of the string.

Species that have not yet been give a species name can have a temporary species name beginning with "sp" and followed by a list of numbers, e.g, Massilia sp900129765. Remove the spXXXXX

To speed up the search, it is recommended that these temporary species names are removed.


```{r}

# load trimmed object
df_trimmed <- readRDS(file = "./objects/taxa.dataframes.precleaned.trimmed.rds")

# find taxa with orphans

matches <- df_trimmed[grepl("(^| )[A-Z]{1,3}( |$)", df_trimmed$Species), ]

# View the first few hits
head(matches)

#      Domain         Phylum               Class            Order         Family         Genus
# 61  Bacteria Proteobacteria Alphaproteobacteria      Rhizobiales   Rhizobiaceae    Aureimonas
# 114 Bacteria     Firmicutes             Bacilli  Paenibacillales    NBRC-103111 Paenibacillus
# 314 Bacteria  Cyanobacteria      Cyanobacteriia Cyanobacteriales    Nostocaceae   Tolypothrix
# 408 Bacteria Proteobacteria Gammaproteobacteria  Pseudomonadales Halomonadaceae     Halomonas
# 419 Bacteria     Firmicutes             Bacilli       Bacillales      DSM-18226      Bacillus
# 420 Bacteria     Firmicutes             Bacilli       Bacillales      DSM-18226      Bacillus
#                         Species
# 61     Aureimonas A sp001425485
# 114 Paenibacillus E sp008017805
# 314   Tolypothrix B sp002368435
# 408     Halomonas C sp900961225
# 419     Bacillus BU sp000242895
# 420     Bacillus BU sp000242895


## Run the function to clean orphaned letters from species
# arguments: df, target_col, max_letters = 3
  
# Regex components:
# (^| ) specifies the start of the string OR a space before the letters.
# [A-Z]{1,3} Matches: one, two or 3 UPPERCASE letters
# ( |$) Requires the letters to be followed by either a space or end of string

#### Detection example
  # | Text              | Detected? |
  # | ----------------- | --------- |
  # | `"Bacteria A"`    | Yes       |
  # | `"A Bacteria"`    | Yes       |
  # | `"Bacteria AB"`   | Yes       |
  # | `"Bacteria ABC"`  | Yes       |
  # | `"Bacteria ABCD"` | No        |
  # | `"Bacteria abc"`  | No        |


results <- lpsn_utils$clean_orphaned_letters(
  df_trimmed,     # data frame
  "Species",      # column name
  max_letters = 3 # max number of sequential UPPERCASE letters
  )

# message
# Cleaning complete. 13 rows modified.

# Report of changes
report_species <- results$report

# Check the first 6 changes
head(report_species)
#   Row_Index                    Original                   Cleaned
# 1        61    Aureimonas A sp001425485    Aureimonas sp001425485
# 2       114 Paenibacillus E sp008017805 Paenibacillus sp008017805
# 3       314   Tolypothrix B sp002368435   Tolypothrix sp002368435
# 4       408     Halomonas C sp900961225     Halomonas sp900961225
# 5       419     Bacillus BU sp000242895      Bacillus sp000242895
# 6       420     Bacillus BU sp000242895      Bacillus sp000242895

# assign the updated data to the original dataframe
df_trimmed <- results$data

# check specific row number to confirm change. eg row index 23
print(df_trimmed)[23,]

#      Domain           Phylum         Class               Order          Family        Genus
# 23 Bacteria Actinobacteriota Actinomycetia Propionibacteriales Nocardioidaceae Unclassified
#         Species
# 23 Unclassified


# save report as csv if needed - as a log of changes from function
utils::write.csv(
  report_species,
  file = "species_cleaning_report.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)


# check for short taxa names and taxa with numbers

species_check <- lpsn_utils$find_suspicious_taxa(
    df = df_trimmed,
    target_col = "Species",
    min_letters = 6,
    export_csv = TRUE,
    file = "species_suspicious_taxa.csv"
)

# 225 suspicious unique taxa identified in 'Species'.

```


### STEP 3: Clean Genus column 

Check if any single, double or triple string in genus column.
Look for a space, exactly one uppercase letter, followed by a space or the end of the string
Check taxa and remove any genus with numbers in the name (e.g. placeholder names)

```{r}

# load data
df_trimmed <- readRDS(file = "./objects/taxonomy.species.fixed.rds")

# find taxa with orphans

matches <- df_trimmed[grepl("(^| )[A-Z]{1,3}( |$)", df_trimmed$Genus), ]

# View the first few hits
head(matches)

#       Domain        Phylum          Class            Order               Family               Genus
# 672 Bacteria Cyanobacteria Cyanobacteriia Cyanobacteriales Chroococcidiopsaceae Crinalium SAG 22.89
#                  Species
# 672 Crinalium epipsammum


## Run the function to clean orphaned letters from genus
# arguments: df, target_col, max_letters = 3
  
# Regex components:
# (^| ) specifies the start of the string OR a space before the letters.
# [A-Z]{1,3} Matches: one, two or 3 UPPERCASE letters
# ( |$) Requires the letters to be followed by either a space or end of string

#### Detection example
  # | Text              | Detected? |
  # | ----------------- | --------- |
  # | `"Bacteria A"`    | Yes       |
  # | `"A Bacteria"`    | Yes       |
  # | `"Bacteria AB"`   | Yes       |
  # | `"Bacteria ABC"`  | Yes       |
  # | `"Bacteria ABCD"` | No        |
  # | `"Bacteria abc"`  | No        |


results <- lpsn_utils$clean_orphaned_letters(
  df_trimmed,     # data frame
  "Genus",      # column name
  max_letters = 3 # max number of sequential UPPERCASE letters
  )

# number of orphaned letters found
# Cleaning complete. 2 rows modified..

# Report of changes
report_genus <- results$report

# Quick look at the top of the report in the console
head(report_genus)

#   Row_Index            Original         Cleaned
# 1       672 Crinalium SAG 22.89 Crinalium 22.89

# assign the updated data to the original dataframe
df_trimmed <- results$data

# check specific row number to confirm change. eg row index 672
print(df_trimmed)[672,]
#       Domain        Phylum          Class            Order               Family           Genus
# 672 Bacteria Cyanobacteria Cyanobacteriia Cyanobacteriales Chroococcidiopsaceae Crinalium 22.89
#                  Species
# 672 Crinalium epipsammum

# save report as csv if needed - as a log of changes from function
utils::write.csv(
  report_genus,
  file = "genus_cleaning_report.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)


# check for short taxa names and taxa with numbers

genus_check <- lpsn_utils$find_suspicious_taxa(
    df = df_trimmed,
    target_col = "Genus",
    min_letters = 7,
    export_csv = TRUE,
    file = "genus_suspicious_taxa.csv"
)

# 121 suspicious unique taxa identified in 'Genus'.

# list unique instances of suspicious taxa
# Please NOTE: taxa can be prefixed with Candidatus, 
# so the list returned should be checked before taxa names are changed
unique_gen <- unique(genus_check$report$Taxon)

# I want the list printed with no row index:
cat(unique_gen, sep = "\n")
```

### STEP 4: Clean Family column 

Check if any single, double or triple string in family column.
Look for a space, exactly one uppercase letter, followed by a space or the end of the string
Check taxa and remove any family with numbers in the name (e.g. placeholder names)

```{r}
# load object 
df_trimmed <- readRDS(df_trimmed, file = "taxonomy.genus.fixed.rds")


# find taxa with orphans

# View the first few hits
head(matches)

# No taxa names with orphans

# [1] Domain  Phylum  Class   Order   Family  Genus   Species
# <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

############### Do not complete the following:
## Run the function to clean orphaned letters from family
# arguments: df, target_col, max_letters = 3
  
# Regex components:
# (^| ) specifies the start of the string OR a space before the letters.
# [A-Z]{1,3} Matches: one, two or 3 UPPERCASE letters
# ( |$) Requires the letters to be followed by either a space or end of string

#### Detection example
  # | Text              | Detected? |
  # | ----------------- | --------- |
  # | `"Bacteria A"`    | Yes       |
  # | `"A Bacteria"`    | Yes       |
  # | `"Bacteria AB"`   | Yes       |
  # | `"Bacteria ABC"`  | Yes       |
  # | `"Bacteria ABCD"` | No        |
  # | `"Bacteria abc"`  | No        |


results <- lpsn_utils$clean_orphaned_letters(
  df_trimmed,     # data frame
  "Family",      # column name
  max_letters = 3 # max number of sequential UPPERCASE letters
  )


# Report of changes
report_family <- results$report

# Quick look at the top of the report in the console
head(report_family)



# assign the updated data to the original dataframe
df_trimmed <- results$data

# check specific row number to confirm change. eg row index 1752
print(df_trimmed)[1752,]


# save report as csv if needed - as a log of changes from function

  report_family,
  file = "family_cleaning_report.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# LSPN API

Register with  the LPSN site and record the login email and password used
https://sso.dsmz.de/auth/realms/DSMZ/login-actions/registration?client_id=api.lpsn&tab_id=4jgxLa3kKA8 

Ensure your .Renviron file contains the fields below to enable login and not record password in the script. Info on modifying .Renviron file: https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/ide/guide/environments/r/managing-r.html 

Format needed for LPSN login:
DSMZ_API_USER = <email>
DSMZ_API_PASSWORD = <password>

```{r}
  "Proteobacteria", # FAIL API LIMIT Correct name: Pseudomonadota (P)

  "Verrucomicrobiota" # PASS Verrucomicrobiota (P)
)

  "Anaerolineae" # correct name (c)
)


order_list <- c(

  "Clostridiales",#  synonym, Correct name: Eubacteriales (O)
  "Absconditicoccus", # preferred name Candidatus Absconditicoccus, wrong level (G)
  "Glutamicibacillocter", # does not exist
  "Eubacteriales", # correct name (O)
  "ubacteriales", # misspelling (O)

  "Candidatus Macinerneyibacteriales" # pro-correct name (C)
)

  "Lactobacteriaceae", # preferred name (F)

)

)

)

  order = order_list,
  family = family_list,
  genus = genus_list,

)


# Output directory structure
```

```{r}
  "Bacillaceae", #correct name (F)
  "Deltabacteria", #PASS synonym,  Correct name: Deltaproteobacteria (C) 
  "Glutamicibacillocter", # FAIL does not exist
  "Prochlorophyceae", # synonym (and no standing), Correct name: Chroococcophycea (C)   "Acidilutibacteraceae", # correct name (F)
  "Glycocaulis", # correct name (G)
  "Porifericola", # preferred name (G)
  "Clostridium", # correct name (G)
  "Curtissbacteria", # misspelling, wrong level, Pro-correct name: "Candidatus Curtissiibacteriota" (P)
  "Glutamicicillocter", # does not exist
  "Acidilutibacter cellobiosedens" # correct name (GS)
)


# Output directory structure
CSV_DIR <- "./results/lpsn_nolevels/csv_lineages"
WB_PATH <- "./results/lpsn_nolevels/LPSN_result_Master.xlsx"
LOG_DIR <- "./results/lpsn_nolevels/logs"

result <- lpsn_utils$lpsn_no_rank_search(
  taxa_names    = taxa_names,
  csv_path      = CSV_DIR,
  workbook_path = WB_PATH,
  log_path      = LOG_DIR
)
```

### Combine log files
This file lists all the taxa that were not found  - these taxa can be searched for using the LPSN site or other database as suitable.
The placeholder names from various databases end up here as they do not exist in the official lineage


```{r}

# set location of log files to combined and where the output should be

log_dir <- "./results/XXXX/logs"
output_file <- "./results/all_missing_taxa.txt"

# List all .txt files in the directory
files <- list.files(path = log_dir, pattern = "\\.txt$", full.names = TRUE)

# Read all files into a single list, merge, and save
merged_content <- files |>
  # Read each file as a character vector
  lapply(readLines, warn = FALSE) |>
  # Flatten the list into one long vector
  unlist() |>
  # Optional: Remove any empty strings and duplicates
  unique() |>
  (\(x) x[x != ""])() |>
  # Sort alphabetically
  sort()

# Write the final combined file
writeLines(merged_content, output_file)

message("Merged ", length(files), " files into: ", output_file)

# Merged 47 files into: /results/all_missing_taxa.txt

```



### Combine all batch results into a single file

```{r}
library(openxlsx)
library(dplyr)

# Set input and output files
input_workbook <- "./results/LPSN_result_Master_20260422_1514.xlsx"
output_csv     <- "./results/LPSN_Master_Combined.csv"

# Get names of all sheets in the workbook
sheet_names <- openxlsx::getSheetNames(input_workbook)

# Read, convert to character, and combine
combined_data <- sheet_names |>
  lapply(\(s) {
    df <- openxlsx::read.xlsx(input_workbook, sheet = s)
    # Convert every column to character to prevent type mismatch
    df |> dplyr::mutate(across(everything(), as.character))
  }) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

# Save to CSV (or use sep = "\t" for TSV)
write.csv(combined_data, output_csv, row.names = FALSE)

message("Successfully combined ", length(sheet_names), " sheets into: ", output_csv)

# Successfully combined 47 sheets into: XXXXX/results/LPSN_Master_Combined_XXXX.csv

```


### Process automated taxonomy lineage update - lookup

A new table is created that uses the returned LPSN names and maps them to the original taxonomy table containing ASVs. The result is Final_Taxonomy_Matched.csv which contains the ASVs, the original lineage, then a column indicating which term in the lineage was matched in the LPSN database and all upstream levels.

This file allows you to check manually & curate the taxonomic lineage as desired. The file used needs to be split into the taxonomic lineage levels.
You can choose to use the taxonomic file that has been cleaned of formatting errors or just the file that has been split without cleaning. 

```{r}

###### usage example
# Define Paths and file names
master_file <- "./results/LPSN_Master_Combined.csv"
tax_file    <- "./taxonomy_pre_LPSN.csv" # the taxa file to use as original copy
result_file <- "./Final_Taxonomy_Matched.csv"

#Define Custom Ranks/Columns (Optional) ---
# You can provide these in any case (lower, UPPER, Sentence)

# rank order to check
my_check_ranks <- c("species", "genus", "family", "order", "class", "phylum", "kingdom")

# columns from the LPSN master file to add to the taxonomy file
my_append_cols <- c("domain", "kingdom", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus", "species")

#call and Run the Function ---
lpsn_utils$process_taxonomy_lookup(
  master_path = master_file,
  taxonomy_path = tax_file,
  output_path = result_file,
  check_ranks = my_check_ranks, # Now an input
  append_cols = my_append_cols  # Now an input
)

# Done. Results in: XXXXX/Final_Taxonomy_Matched.csv
```
